text.content: Why human oversight is an architectural decision

rich_text.plain_text: Why human oversight is an architectural decision

text.content: Contigo GmbH's support agent can now retrieve information, invoke tools, and enforce grounding behaviour with no human involvement. For the majority of client interactions — answering product questions, checking eligibility criteria, performing calculations. Full autonomy is the correct design. Human review of every interaction would eliminate the operational benefit of automation entirely.

For the majority of client interactions — answering product questions, checking eligibility criteria, performing calculations. Full autonomy is the correct design. Human review of every interaction would eliminate the operational benefit of automation entirely.

text.content: But Contigo also handles loan application status queries. These return live client-specific data from a tracked system. Before that data is retrieved and presented to a client, one question should always be answered first: is the agent about to query the correct application?

rich_text.plain_text: But Contigo also handles loan application status queries. These return live client-specific data from a tracked system. Before that data is retrieved and presented to a client, one question should always be answered first: is the agent about to query the correct application?

text.content: A miscommunication about a reference number (the client says APP-9921 but means APP-9291) results in the wrong client's application status being retrieved and presented. In a regulated financial services environment that is not a UX failure. It is a data protection incident.

text.content: This is the case for a human checkpoint. Not because the agent cannot be trusted to invoke the tool correctly, but because the consequence of invoking it incorrectly is significant enough that a confirmation step before execution is justified.

text.content: What this means for your current Chatflow

rich_text.plain_text: What this means for your current Chatflow

text.content: What is available is a system prompt instruction that directs the agent to ask the client to confirm the application reference before invoking the loan status tool. The agent should comply consistently but cannot be guaranteed to do so in the way a deterministic infrastructure constraint can.

The agent should comply consistently but cannot be guaranteed to do so in the way a deterministic infrastructure constraint can.

text.content: The practical value of implementing this now is threefold. It introduces the confirmation pattern into the agent's behaviour at a level the current environment supports. It gives you experience writing an invocation condition that requires parameter verification before execution. And it accurately represents the design intent of HITL (pre-execution confirmation) even if the mechanism is softer than a full approval gate.

text.content: Before invoking the loan status lookup tool, always confirm the application reference with the client. Ask: "Just to confirm, the application reference you would like me to check is [reference]. Is that correct?" Wait for the client's explicit confirmation before proceeding. text.content: This test is an honest demonstration of the difference between a soft instruction and a hard constraint. Observing this difference now is the most direct way to understand why true HITL requires infrastructure enforcement rather than prompt governance.

text.content: Human in the loop is about matching the level of oversight to the consequence of proceeding without it. A confirmation step in the system prompt brings the right design intent into your current Chatflow.
